data.description:
## Context
The prior tickets-history reclaim claimed a fresh unfiltered clone ceiling of 150 MiB, but its executable acceptance measured only .git/objects/pack/*.pack. The rewritten baseline tree itself was already 290,690,203 logical bytes. A current fresh single-branch clone is 1,186,317,529 logical bytes / 1,475,424,256 allocated bytes while its pack is only 322.57 MiB. The pack-only metric therefore cannot detect checkout payload or small-file allocation growth. Discovered during absurd-zoometric-bobwhite.

## Plan
- Define separate authoritative metrics for reachable pack bytes, checked-out logical bytes, checked-out allocated bytes, file count/block slack, and total fresh-clone footprint.
- Measure them from a fresh unfiltered single-branch tickets clone with platform-tolerant reporting.
- Add enforceable budgets and trend evidence at an operation-linked or in-process seam, with CI as an optional trigger rather than the only trigger.
- Correct operator documentation so pack size is never described as whole-clone size.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each size layer has an unambiguous definition and reproducible measurement.
- [ ] A regression fixture where pack bytes pass but checkout or allocated bytes fail is detected.
- [ ] Budget enforcement is portable to projects without this repository CI provider.
- [ ] Reclaim and capacity documentation distinguish pack, tree, and whole-clone claims.
data.title: Enforce whole tickets-store footprint budgets beyond Git pack bytes
